## Why This Is Asked

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to negotiate across orgs and with external vendors under tight constraints, focusing on preparation, stakeholder alignment, and ongoing feedback.

## Key Concepts

- Stakeholder alignment
- Negotiation framework (BATNA, WATNA, ZOPA)
- Scope definition and acceptance criteria
- Vendor relationships and structured feedback loops

## Code Example

```javascript
const negotiationPlan = {
  objective: "Deliver MVP dataset by date",
  milestones: ["Core data", "QA pass", "Delivery complete"],
  acceptance: { quality: 5.0, latency: "2h", errorRate: "<1%" },
  tradeoffs: ["scope vs. cost", "speed vs. quality"]
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- What data would you collect to justify the staged scope and trigger milestones?
- How would you document and socialize the final agreement to avoid scope creep?

- Rollout strategy: canaries, feature flags, governance

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question probes real-world conflict resolution across product, safety/privacy, and regulatory concerns, focusing on negotiation scaffolding and adaptability under uncertainty.

## Key Concepts
- Interest-based negotiation
- Stakeholder mapping and trade-off analysis
- Data minimization and privacy-by-design
- Feedback loops and post-release iteration
- On-device processing vs. cloud telemetry

## Code Example
```javascript
function surfaceInterests(stakeholders){
  // gather needs and constraints from each party
  const needs = stakeholders.map(s => s.needs);
  return Array.from(new Set(needs.flat())).sort();
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you measure success if the pilot reveals higher privacy risk than expected?
- What would trigger a rollback and how would you communicate it?

## Why This Is Asked

Assesses ability to structure high-stakes multi-party negotiations, surface underlying interests, and codify accountable actions with measurable deadlines.

## Key Concepts

- Interests vs. positions
- Option framing and trade-offs
- Blameless incident handling
- Telemetry-driven decision making

```json
  "plan": {
    "option": "Safe phased rollout",
    "owners": {"Eng": "Lead", "Prod": "Owner", "Sales": "Owner"},
    "deadlines": ["2026-03-15", "2026-03-17"],
    "checkpoints": [{"time": "24h", "metric": "error_rate<1%"}]
  }
}
```

- How do you handle a stakeholder who refuses to commit to a deadline?
- What signals would trigger aborting the rollout?
